question: If remembrance alone destroys sin, why should one still perform expiation rites for the sake of others?
premises: Remembrance of the Lord is said to destroy sin.
Some practitioners do not know the highest truth.
The revered Picu scripture still prescribes ritual action for their grace.
inference: Even when remembrance suffices in principle, expiation rites are performed to support those who lack full knowledge of the truth.
uncertainties: The exact identity or scope of 'śrīpicau' is not specified in this verse.
plain_english: Even so, for the grace of those who do not know the truth, one should act as taught in the revered Picu scripture. But if remembrance alone destroys sin, O Lord, how can an expiation rite still be prescribed?
